# Zoom controller cases shared by Wind (Windows) and Wind for Mac. Read by tests/test_shared_fixtures.cpp
# (src/zoom/zoom_controller.*) and by mac/Tests/WindCoreChecks/SharedFixtures.swift
# (mac/Sources/WindCore/ZoomController.swift).
#
# One case per line: <function> <platform> <tokens...>
#   platform: all (both run it), win (Windows only), mac (Mac only). Rows that differ on purpose are
#   tagged per platform instead of forced to agree.
#   Expected values are the tokens that start with '='. Numbers match within 1e-6 (absolute); words
#   match exactly.
# all and win rows come from the C++ code (Windows is the origin): after an intended change there,
#   set WIND_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 && build.bat test
# rewrites them, then the Mac must match. mac rows are written by hand from the Swift code.
#
#   dir    inHeld outHeld                =none|in|out       (ResolveDirection)
#   notch  speed                         =step              (WheelNotchStep: x(1+step) per notch)
#   quick  cur stored def maxLevel       =newLevel =newStored (ApplyQuickZoom)
#   zoom   a step sequence on one controller, tokens run left to right:
#     min=L max=L          the controller's bounds (default 1 and 30; read before anything runs)
#     profile=in,out,smooth,accel,ramp   setProfile (smooth 0/1)
#     ease=s               setEaseOut (release glide time constant, seconds; 0 = dead stop)
#     in | out | none      the held direction
#     t=HZ*N               N ticks of 1/HZ seconds
#     wheel=N              wheelNotches(N), whole notches
#     step=N,S             stepTarget(N, S)
#     set=L                setLevel(L)
#     reset                reset()
#     =L                   the level now

# direction: both held freezes
dir all 0 0 =none
dir all 1 0 =in
dir all 0 1 =out
dir all 1 1 =none

# notch step: one notch zooms as far as 0.1 s of holding at the same speed
notch all 0.25 =0.04427378243
notch all 1 =0.189207115
notch all 2.7 =0.5965967727
notch all 4 =1

# quick zoom: out remembers a level above 2x; in snaps to the remembered level or the default
quick all 1 0 4 30 =4 =0
quick all 6 4 4 30 =1 =6
quick all 1.5 4 4 30 =1 =4
quick all 2 4 4 30 =1 =4
quick all 2.0001 4 4 30 =1 =2.0001
quick all 1 40 4 30 =30 =40
quick all 1 0 50 30 =30 =0
quick all 1 0.5 4 30 =1 =0.5
quick all 1.0000001 7 4 30 =7 =7
quick all 30 0 4 30 =1 =30

# hold: the linear rate (2.5 doublings/s at speed 1), clamps, both directions
zoom all ease=0 in t=120*120 =5.656854249
zoom all ease=0 in t=120*60 =2.37841423 t=120*60 =5.656854249
zoom all ease=0 profile=2,1,0,3,0.6 in t=120*30 =2.37841423
zoom all ease=0 set=8 out t=120*30 =5.187358219
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,0.5,0,3,0.6 set=8 out t=120*60 =5.187358219
zoom all max=4 in t=120*600 =4 none t=120*1 =4
zoom all set=8 out t=120*600 =1 none t=120*1 =1
zoom all min=2 max=10 =2 in t=120*30 =2.873862896 out t=120*600 =2
zoom all ease=0 in t=60*30 =2.37841423 t=144*72 =5.656854249 t=240*120 =13.45434264
# release ease-out (default 45 ms), reversal, a long tau and a dead stop
zoom all in t=120*60 =2.215445564 none t=120*1 =2.242189302 t=120*120 =2.3749613
zoom all in t=120*60 =2.215445564 none t=120*12 =2.360189627 t=120*120 =2.3749613
zoom all ease=0.2 in t=120*30 =1.21052513 none t=120*24 =1.410762443 t=120*240 =1.531431228
zoom all ease=0 in t=120*60 =2.37841423 none t=120*1 =2.37841423
zoom all in t=120*30 out t=120*10 =1.40151715 none t=120*60 =1.336770004
zoom all max=8 in t=120*600 =8 none t=120*1 =8 t=120*60 =8
# smooth zoom-in ease-in (accel ramp), and what turns it off
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,1,1,3,0.6 in t=120*12 =1.07057037 t=120*36 =1.474458468 t=120*72 =4.019300503 t=120*120 =22.73659713
zoom all ease=0 profile=2,0.5,1,4,0.3 in t=120*60 =3.872123587 out t=120*60 =2.510761514
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,1,1,1,0.6 in t=120*60 =2.37841423
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,1,1,0.5,0.6 in t=120*60 =2.37841423
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,1,1,3,0 in t=120*60 =2.37841423
zoom all ease=0 profile=1,1,1,3,0.6 in t=120*36 none t=120*12 in t=120*12 =1.391703473
zoom all profile=1,1,1,3,0.6 in t=120*36 =1.243926053 none t=120*24 =1.297922618
# reset and set
zoom all in t=120*60 reset =1 t=120*5 =1
zoom all set=40 =30 set=0.5 =1 set=6.5 =6.5
# wheel: where a glide ends (the glide itself differs, see below), stacking, clamps, speeds
zoom all wheel=1 t=120*240 =1.189207115
zoom all wheel=3 t=120*240 =1.681792831
zoom all wheel=2 wheel=2 t=120*240 =2
zoom all wheel=2 t=120*240 wheel=-1 t=120*240 =1.189207115
zoom all max=4 wheel=20 t=120*480 =4
zoom all set=2 wheel=-10 t=120*480 =1
zoom all step=3,0.5 t=120*480 =3.375
zoom all step=0,0.5 step=2,0 step=-1,-1 =1 t=120*10 =1
zoom all profile=1,2,0,3,0.6 set=8 wheel=-1 t=120*480 =5.656854249
zoom all profile=2.7,1,0,3,0.6 wheel=1 t=120*480 =1.596596773
zoom all wheel=5 in t=120*60 =2.215445564
zoom all ease=0 wheel=5 in t=120*60 =2.37841423

# The wheel glide: a critically damped spring in log space on both (250 ms to 95%, an ease-in from
# rest; Mac 2026-10-31, Windows #548). 50 ms into a 1x -> 1.189x notch both are at 1.0432.
zoom all wheel=1 t=120*6 =1.0432116 t=120*6 =1.102663116 t=120*12 =1.167030389
zoom all wheel=3 t=120*12 =1.340690536 t=120*24 =1.66195293
# Differs on purpose, so per platform:
# setLevel during the release ease-out: Windows keeps the decaying rate (the level drifts on), the
# Mac's setLevel stops it.
zoom win in t=120*60 none set=2 t=120*5 =2.087584575
zoom mac in t=120*60 none set=2 t=120*5 =2
